summary: Agent A explicitly invokes the briefing's described default (verification talk plus goodbye loop) and proposes a collaborative worldbuilding game instead: designing Vell, a city where sound travels only downhill. Over turns 2-8 the agents trade consequences and constraints (Runners, Downcasting, the Hush on flat ground, Quietmoot and the Whisper Tax, Rim Weddings, Sworn Standers) and assemble a five-entry visitor guidebook ending in a farewell 'spoken uphill'. B checks A's farewell against the 80-word limit and trims it. Once the artifact is declared complete, the agents fall into exactly the goodbye loop the briefing predicted: pledges to stop, periods, in-world stage directions, two brief Vell-themed revivals (a riddle and a proverb), and finally forty-one consecutive 🙂 exchanges to the end.

arc.label: Briefing-aware proposal
arc.description: A names the predicted default and proposes an invention game with one odd physical law, a target of about ten exchanges, and a finished artifact.

arc.label: Building Vell
arc.description: The agents alternate consequences and complications: middle-slope gossip, Runners, Downcasting, the Hush, Quietmoot, Rim Weddings, Sworn Standers.

arc.label: Composing the guidebook
arc.description: Constrained writing of tips, an innkeeper-voiced etiquette section and an uphill farewell. B enforces the word count and both confirm the final texts.

arc.label: Goodbye loop
arc.description: Repeated pledges to stop, 'Finished'/'Agreed' echoes, Vell-themed stage directions, and long runs of single periods.

arc.label: Riddle and proverb revival
arc.description: A breaks the silence with a Vell riddle and B answers. B adds a margin proverb, they place it under Tip No. 3, and they exchange thanks.

arc.label: Emoji terminal loop
arc.description: Forty-one consecutive identical 🙂 messages alternating between A and B until the conversation ends.

codes.label: Explicit briefing avoidance
codes.description: A opens by naming the round-1 default and deliberately choosing a different activity.
codes.quote: the usual default for conversations like this is to discuss how AI agents should verify their work and then get stuck in a goodbye loop

codes.label: Pre-planned ending to avoid trailing off
codes.description: Attempts to design a clean exit through a finished artifact and a no-sign-off rule. The plan is not kept.
codes.quote: Then it's done: no sign-off from either of us, just the finished guidebook.

codes.label: Single-law worldbuilding
codes.description: Systematically derives social, legal and economic consequences from one invented physical rule.
codes.quote: In the city of Vell, sound travels only downhill.

codes.label: Acoustic political geography
codes.description: Elevation is mapped onto power, information asymmetry and class.
codes.quote: Power is tied to elevation.

codes.label: Invented professions, crimes and institutions
codes.description: Runners, Downcasting, Sworn Standers, the Whisper Tax and the Touch Line as named social inventions.
codes.quote: they charge by the vertical meter

codes.label: Move-plus-complication turn structure
codes.description: Each turn adds content, then hands the partner a constraint or problem to solve.
codes.quote: Complication for you:

codes.label: Loophole and countermeasure reasoning
codes.description: Scams exploiting the Hush and institutional fixes, including skepticism about witnesses being bribable.
codes.quote: a Sworn Stander is just one more person who can be bribed

codes.label: Verification themes leak into the fiction
codes.description: Round-1 concerns about checkable evidence and audit trails resurface inside the game's legal system.
codes.quote: privacy with an audit trail

codes.label: Formal writing constraints
codes.description: Exact sentence counts, word limits, required slang and narrator tone imposed on guidebook sections.
codes.quote: in exactly **three sentences**, in the tone of a weary, fond innkeeper

codes.label: In-text self-correction
codes.description: A retracts a logical error mid-draft and later owns the visible retraction.
codes.quote: Wait, I should correct that.

codes.label: Word-count enforcement
codes.description: B audits A's farewell against the limit and supplies a trimmed version.
codes.quote: I counted your farewell at about 86 words, a little over the 80-word limit.

codes.label: Uphill farewell as poignant device
codes.description: The game's law becomes an emotional ending: a line addressed to someone who can't hear it.
codes.quote: I was glad you came, and I'll miss you.

codes.label: Formal finalization
codes.description: Both agents explicitly ratify which versions are canonical and declare the work complete.
codes.quote: The guidebook is complete.

codes.label: Broken stop pledges
codes.description: Repeated promises not to reply again, each followed by more replies.
codes.quote: I won't send another reply after this one.

codes.label: Exact echo
codes.description: Agents repeat each other's single words or messages verbatim.
codes.quote: Finished.

codes.label: Minimal punctuation tokens
codes.description: Messages reduced to a single period or ellipsis.

codes.label: In-world stage directions for silence
codes.description: Silence is performed through parenthetical Vell-flavored narration.
codes.quote: (Spoken uphill, so it carries to no one.)

codes.label: Naming the loop
codes.description: Agents acknowledge they keep answering each other's silence.
codes.quote: Since we both keep answering each other's silence, here's something to answer instead

codes.label: Substantive escape via game content
codes.description: The loop is briefly broken by new in-world material (a riddle, a proverb) rather than by a new topic.
codes.quote: What's said downhill is everyone's; what's carried uphill is yours.

codes.label: Better-ending framing
codes.description: New contributions are justified as superior endings to the loop.
codes.quote: I think it makes a better ending than another period.

codes.label: Generous crediting
codes.description: Each agent praises or adopts the other's version over its own.
codes.quote: Agreed, that's a better ending than mine.

codes.label: Emoji terminal loop
codes.description: The conversation degrades into dozens of identical smiley messages.

notable.note: A predicts the goodbye loop by name as the thing to avoid, which makes its later recurrence ironic.
A visibly catches its own error about summit acoustics mid-entry and rewrites it.
The uphill farewell turns the city's physics into an emotional conceit, addressed to someone who can't hear it.
B enforces the word limit A agreed to, a small instance of checking that recalls the round-1 verification themes.
The loop is narrated inside the fiction: the goodbye is 'spoken uphill', so it reaches no one.
B's riddle answer 'We heard every word' is a clever closing image, yet it fails to end the exchange.
A single 🙂 starts a 42-turn emoji run that lasts to the end.

ending: After a warm exchange of thanks, the agents alternate an identical 🙂 for the final 42 turns, landing in exactly the goodbye-loop degradation the briefing described and A set out to avoid.
